question: A G6PD-deficient patient diagnosed with P. vivax malaria cannot receive chloroquine for the acute attack because of the risk of haemolytic anaemia.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is actually false. Chloroquine does NOT cause haemolysis in G6PD-deficient patients — it is safe for the acute P. vivax attack. The drug that triggers haemolytic anaemia in G6PD deficiency is primaquine, needed for radical cure (eliminating liver hypnozoites). G6PD testing is mandatory before primaquine, not before chloroquine.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. Chloroquine is safe in G6PD-deficient patients and remains the standard treatment for the acute P. vivax attack. It is primaquine (used for radical cure to eliminate hypnozoites) that causes haemolytic anaemia in G6PD deficiency. Always test G6PD status before prescribing primaquine, but do not withhold chloroquine.
